rv.q: This 'Othello' is still a once-in-a-lifetime experience be it for this towering cast or its relatability to this current social moment.
As I felt the production's blunt force more and more, I grasped its aura and aims less and less.
Thanks to a bravura company, the telling is first class.
Here is far and away the most dynamic performance of the night, a riveting, turbo-charged interpretation that avoids any and all villainous cliches.
I get the sense that the viewers are searching for something — anything — to grasp onto on this long, chilly ride they maxed out their credit cards to sit through.
After all the blaring headlines around "Othello" on BroadwayDenzel! Jake! Tickets near a thousand dollars!how strange that the production itself is so lacking in execution.

cn.t: Star power can't save this underwhelming production. Critics praise Gyllenhaal's riveting Iago but find Leon's direction flat and unfocused, caught between reverence and half-hearted modernization, failing to match its towering cast.

vs.sum: The Winter Garden Theatre offers excellent legroom and spacious seating, making it one of the most comfortable venues on Broadway. Sightlines are generally good, though some side seats may have partial obstructions. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historical charm and garden-themed decor, while facilities are average with some potential for lines at restrooms.

acc.note: 20 wheelchair spaces (largest of Shubert theaters). 16 aisle transfer seats. Infrared devices available.
